@graph.name: CA-125 Blood Test
@graph.description: CA-125 (cancer antigen 125) is a serum biomarker that can support evaluation of persistent symptoms suggestive of ovarian pathology and monitoring of selected patients with known epithelial ovarian cancer. It is neither a universal ovarian cancer screening test nor a stand-alone way to diagnose or exclude malignancy.

mainEntity.name: What is the CA-125 test?

acceptedAnswer.text: It measures an antigen associated with MUC16 in blood; it is used as an adjunct in selected ovarian disease pathways.

mainEntity.name: Does CA-125 diagnose ovarian cancer?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Diagnosis requires clinical assessment, imaging and sometimes histopathology.

mainEntity.name: Does a normal CA-125 rule out ovarian cancer?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Early disease and some tumour types may produce normal values.

mainEntity.name: Can endometriosis raise CA-125?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Endometriosis, menstruation and benign pelvic inflammation can raise levels.

mainEntity.name: Can pregnancy elevate CA-125?

acceptedAnswer.text: CA-125 can change in pregnancy, especially early; interpretation must consider gestational state.

mainEntity.name: Can a benign ovarian cyst increase CA-125?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A raised result is not specific for malignancy.

mainEntity.name: Can fibroids raise CA-125?

acceptedAnswer.text: They may contribute in some contexts, but persistent symptoms still require an appropriate pelvic assessment.

mainEntity.name: Is CA-125 a good annual screening test for every woman?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Routine average-risk asymptomatic screening with CA-125 has not shown a suitable benefit–harm balance.

mainEntity.name: What ovarian cancer symptoms should I watch for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Persistent abdominal distension, early satiety, pelvic pain and urinary frequency, especially if new or frequent, deserve evaluation.

mainEntity.name: Why is persistent bloating important?

acceptedAnswer.text: New or frequent distension can be an early symptom of several diseases, including ovarian pathology; it is not specific for cancer.

mainEntity.name: What level of CA-125 is abnormal?

acceptedAnswer.text: The assay reference interval is report-specific. Clinical imaging-referral thresholds are age-specific in the 2026 NICE symptom pathway.

mainEntity.name: What are the 2026 NICE CA-125 referral thresholds?

acceptedAnswer.text: For symptomatic people 40–49 ≥35, 50–59 ≥31, 60–69 ≥24, 70–79 ≥25 and ≥80 years ≥31 IU/mL; they are UK clinical referral thresholds.

mainEntity.name: Why can an older person need ultrasound with CA-125 below 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2026 NICE pathway uses lower age-specific thresholds for certain older age groups.

mainEntity.name: What if I am 39 or younger?

acceptedAnswer.text: CA-125 should not be used alone to decide on ovarian cancer evaluation. Discuss ultrasound for persistent concerning symptoms.

mainEntity.name: Does every high CA-125 require cancer treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. There are many benign causes and treatment must never start from a biomarker alone.

mainEntity.name: What investigation usually follows concerning CA-125?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pelvic/abdominal ultrasound with clinical review; additional imaging or referral depends on findings.

mainEntity.name: Is CA-125 useful for follow-up after ovarian cancer treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Serial testing may help in selected patients under oncology supervision, alongside symptoms and imaging.

mainEntity.name: What if CA-125 increases but imaging is normal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clinical context, assay consistency, alternative causes and safety-net follow-up matter; discuss with the treating specialist.

mainEntity.name: Can CA-125 be high in liver disease?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Liver inflammation or ascites may raise CA-125 without ovarian malignancy.

mainEntity.name: Can infection cause high CA-125?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pelvic or peritoneal inflammation and some infections can increase CA-125.

mainEntity.name: Can CA-125 be high with tuberculosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Peritoneal tuberculosis can occasionally elevate CA-125; it is not a TB-specific test.

mainEntity.name: What is HE4 and ROMA?

acceptedAnswer.text: HE4 is another serum marker, and ROMA is an algorithm combining HE4, CA-125 and menopausal status for selected adnexal mass contexts; neither is universal screening.

mainEntity.name: Is fasting required for CA-125?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fasting is generally unnecessary for an isolated CA-125 test.

mainEntity.name: Should CA-125 be measured during menstruation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Menstruation can raise CA-125. Inform your clinician; collection timing may matter for borderline values.

mainEntity.name: Can a low CA-125 delay a needed scan?

acceptedAnswer.text: It should not. Persistent symptoms and clinical findings take priority over one blood result.

mainEntity.name: Should I repeat CA-125 every month?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no general rule. Repeat frequency depends on the clinical question and oncology plan.

mainEntity.name: Does CA-125 identify the stage of ovarian cancer?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Staging requires specialist evaluation and imaging/surgery as indicated.

mainEntity.name: Can CA-125 detect every gynaecological cancer?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Sensitivity and relevance vary substantially across cancer types and histologies.

mainEntity.name: Can I use CA-125 to check whether abdominal pain is cancer?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It is a selective adjunct; many causes of pain require other tests and imaging.

mainEntity.name: What if symptoms persist despite a normal ultrasound?

acceptedAnswer.text: Seek reassessment and investigate alternative conditions; persistent or worsening symptoms need safety-net follow-up.
